accuracy.evidence: Checked against the Met Office 'Layers of the atmosphere' and 'What is air pressure?' pages, NASA Earth Observatory and NOAA JetStream: dry air is about 78.1% nitrogen, 20.9% oxygen, 0.93% argon and about 0.04% carbon dioxide (so 'under 1 part in 2,000' holds at ~420 ppm); mean sea-level pressure 1013.25 hPa, falling roughly exponentially with an ~8 km scale height (the lab's pAt gives 510 hPa at 5.5 km and 335 hPa at 8.85 km, matching the 'halves every 5.5 km' and 'about a third at Everest' figures); troposphere to about 12 km on average (8 km at the poles, 18 km at the equator) holding nearly all weather; stratosphere to ~50 km with the ozone layer at ~15–35 km absorbing most UV; mesosphere 50–85 km where most meteors burn up; aurora at ~100–300 km and the ISS at ~400 km in the thermosphere; greenhouse effect: ~15 °C global mean vs ~−18 °C effective temperature. Air density ~1.2 kg/m³ at sea level gives the m9 answer 12n kg for 10n m³. Parameterised answers n*78, n*21, n*22 and n*12 are whole numbers at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented KS2 misconceptions about air (Allen, Misconceptions in Primary Science, chapters on air and Earth in space; Driver et al., Making Sense of Secondary Science, 'air and gases'): air being mostly oxygen (prediction, a dedicated miss when the nitrogen count lands near 21, challenge tag oxy, practice p1), air weighing nothing or making things lighter (balance prediction, challenge tags none and wind, mastery m1, adult note on helium), pressure being higher up a mountain because it is nearer the sky (prediction, packet that puffs at the top, challenge tags sea and cave, m2), weather happening high up (layer prediction, cloud card feedback, challenge tags strat and space), and Earth being hotter with no air because nothing blocks the Sun (prediction, blanket-off thermometer at −18 °C, challenge tags hot and same, m4).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagatmos is built on this topic's own mechanisms: a 100-square air jar whose counts lock only near 78 and 21 and recognise the oxygen swap, a beam balance that tips with each pump of air and levels when it is let out, a mountain whose sealed packet and air-dot cloud change size with a pressure model (1013 e^(−h/8) hPa), a four-band atmosphere whose cards carry their real heights, and an ozone arc that shortens UV rays plus a blanket switch that moves the global mean between 15 °C and −18 °C. It is not the flagair lab (475, air takes up space and moves things, ages 3–5) or the flagwxclim/flagwind weather labs; the gate reports under 30% shingle overlap with every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea is met through the task before the text states it: the jar refuses 21 for nitrogen and shows how little room is left after 78 and 21; the beam goes down on the pumped side, so air has weight; the packet visibly puffs as the climber rises and the hPa readout falls, then squashes on the way down; cards bounce off wrong layers with the height that rules them out; switching the blanket off drops the thermometer to −18 °C while the Sun still shines. Each step summary appears only once its task is done.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: most of the air (oxygen tempts; the jar locks nitrogen at 78), pumping a balloon on a balance (stays level tempts; the pumped side goes down), where pressure is highest (top of the mountain tempts; the readout and packet show sea level), where weather happens (every layer the same tempts; cloud cards only fit the troposphere), and Earth with no air (hotter, nothing would block the Sun tempts; the thermometer falls to −18 °C). The task message echoes the locked-in choice via A.reveal.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with two wrong options each, every one mapped to its own message: oxy, co2, none, wind, sea, cave, strat, space, ozrain, ozhold, hot and same, e.g. 'cave': 'Going down, more air is above you, so the pressure goes up, not down.' and 'hot': 'Sunlight would still reach the ground, but the heat would escape to space. Earth would average about −18 °C.' In-lab misses name the slip too, e.g. '21 is about how much oxygen there is. Nitrogen is far more: nearly 4 in every 5 squares.'

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes the learner limits: kid text reads at about FK grade 3 and adult text at about grade 7 (the long mistakes paragraph was split on the first pass, from grade 17.5 to 6). Kid sentences are short and concrete ('Air is matter, so it has weight.'), and the precise KS2/KS3 words are used and explained: atmosphere, nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, air pressure, sea level, troposphere, stratosphere, ozone layer, UV.

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches and explanation overlap with every other lesson is under 12%. Each lab step has one job (composition, weight, pressure with height, layers, shield and blanket) and every feedback line carries a number, a height or a layer name. Item explanations give the reason (less air above, heat escapes to space) instead of restating the question.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px in light and dark themes on every step, before and after Show me. First-pass fixes: the pressure readout and 'sea level' line were clipped at the right edge and the climber was hidden behind the feedback box (mountain and readouts moved up and in), the balance caption sat under the feedback box (stand raised), the troposphere band was covered by three-line feedback (bands now end at 70% height), and 'UV reaching the ground' and 'heat blanket on' were clipped (shortened). Buttons wrap two to a row and stay full-size; the canvas keeps a light card in dark mode.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: '− 10', '− 1', '+ 1', '+ 10' and 'That much' for the air jar, 'Pump' and 'Let the air out', 'Climb 1 km' and 'Go down 1 km', one button per layer naming the card, and 'Add ozone layer', 'Blanket off', 'Blanket on', each with an aria-label. The canvas aria-label reports the state after every move ('5.3 km up, air pressure about 522 hPa.'), and challenge feedback is an aria-live status. walk.cjs reports axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
